ppl-kom-1.title: PPL Kom-1
ppl-kom-1.alt: Aerodrome circuit with lettered callouts A to G. Open the full-size figure to inspect the labels.
ppl-kom-1.context: Original PPL Kom-1 circuit diagram from the Serbian CAA Communications appendix, page 23. A points to the apron with parked aircraft. B points to the taxiway holding point before the runway. C points to the line-up position at the start of the runway. D points to the crosswind side of the circuit. E points to the downwind side, parallel to the runway and opposite the landing direction. F points to the base leg, perpendicular to the runway before the turn onto final. G points to final approach aligned with the runway before its threshold. The aircraft on the downwind side travels from right to left; final and runway travel is left to right.

ppl-pof-1.title: PPL PoF-1
ppl-pof-1.sourceLabel: Serbian CAA · Principles of Flight appendix · page 24
ppl-pof-1.alt: PPL PoF-1: original examination figure with its source labels.
ppl-pof-1.context: PPL PoF-1 plots bank angle in degrees on the horizontal axis (Nagib vazduhoplova) and load factor on the vertical axis (Koeficijent opterecenja). For a coordinated level turn the curve follows n=1/cos(bank): 20 degrees approximately 1.064, 50 degrees approximately 1.556, 60 degrees 2, 66 degrees approximately 2.46, 75 degrees approximately 3.86. Readings are approximate; do not describe 75 degrees as an exact permissible bank for a 3.8 limit.

ppl-pof-2.title: PPL PoF-2
ppl-pof-2.sourceLabel: Serbian CAA · Principles of Flight appendix · page 24
ppl-pof-2.alt: PPL PoF-2: original examination figure with its source labels.
ppl-pof-2.context: PPL PoF-2 is a wing polar with lift coefficient Cy vertically and drag coefficient Cx horizontally. Point 3 is the leftmost portion of the polar, minimum drag. Point 4 is the tangent from the origin, best lift/drag ratio. Point 6 is the maximum lift coefficient, critical angle of attack. Other points 1, 2, 5 and 7 are retained.

ppl-op-1.title: PPL OP-1
ppl-op-1.sourceLabel: Serbian CAA · Operational Procedures appendix · page 23
ppl-op-1.alt: PPL OP-1: original examination figure with its source labels.
ppl-op-1.context: PPL OP-1 airport diagram: A marks the displaced-threshold runway portion before B, usable for taxi and takeoff but not landing touchdown. B marks the landing threshold. C marks a closed runway with crosses. E is the chevron-marked overrun beyond runway end D. Do not confuse B with E: question OPERATIONAL-PROCEDURES-115 asks about A and B but its stored answer describes A and E, so flag this wording discrepancy.

questionNotes.OPERATIONAL-PROCEDURES-115: Source wording discrepancy: the question asks about A and B, but its stored correct answer describes A and E. The original diagram is shown unchanged.

ppl-op-4.title: PPL OP-4
ppl-op-4.sourceLabel: Serbian CAA · Operational Procedures appendix · page 25
ppl-op-4.alt: PPL OP-4: original examination figure with its source labels.
ppl-op-4.context: PPL OP-4 is reproduced in monochrome in the source. A is a square with diagonal cross (the red panel/yellow cross described in the question prohibits landing). B is a square with one diagonal (special care on approach and landing). C is the reporting office C sign. D is a plain dumbbell (land, take off and taxi on runways/taxiways). E is a dumbbell with black bars through its circular ends (land and take off on runways; other ground movement need not be confined to runways/taxiways). F is a landing T, toward its crossbar. G is an unserviceability cross. H is a double cross indicating gliding activity. I is a right-angled arrow indicating right-hand circuits.
ppl-op-4.note: The original appendix reproduces these signals in monochrome; use the colours stated in the question.
